expectedBehavior.rule: An AssetStatePeriod represents a time span during which an asset has the same Quantity, Amount, and Mrr. An asset has as many state periods as there are asset actions (changes) during its lifecycle.
expectedBehavior.source: Salesforce Revenue Cloud (RLM) Developer Guide - AssetStatePeriod object reference (developer.salesforce.com .../sforce_api_objects_assetstateperiod.htm)

expectedBehavior.rule: On an amendment (upsell/downsell/qty or field change), the prior state period is closed (EndDate truncated to the amendment effective date boundary) and a NEW state period is created starting at/after the effective date carrying the changed Quantity/Mrr; the change is effective-dated so future-dated amendments create the split at that future boundary.
expectedBehavior.source: Trailhead 'Managing Customer Asset Amendments in Revenue Cloud' + Salesforce Help 'Amending, Renewing, and Canceling Assets' (a new asset state period reflecting the updated quantity is created; original state remains closed as of the amendment date; effective date governs when the change/boundary occurs)

expectedBehavior.rule: A renewal creates a NEW forward-dated state period (starting after the prior period's EndDate) with uplifted price (PriceRevisionPolicy); a cancellation does NOT create a new state period (it closes the asset lifecycle).
expectedBehavior.source: Trailhead 'Manage Customer Asset Renewals and Cancellations' + repo prior research Jira/Task/sc3419 .../W1_rlm_asset_lifecycle.md and OFFICIAL_RCA_REFERENCES.md

expectedBehavior.rule: EndDate=null on the LAST state period is expected ONLY for evergreen subscriptions; termed assets should have a bounded EndDate on every period.
expectedBehavior.source: Salesforce Object/RLM Reference - AssetStatePeriod EndDate: 'On an asset that is an evergreen subscription, the last asset state period has no end date.'

expectedBehavior.rule: SegmentType is a picklist whose default value is Yearly (other values Custom/FreeTrial/Prorated); it should be populated on generated state periods.
expectedBehavior.source: Salesforce RLM AssetStatePeriod object reference (SegmentType default = Yearly) + FortraUAT sobject describe

expectedBehavior.rule: State periods for a single asset should partition its lifecycle contiguously and NOT overlap (each period is a distinct non-overlapping time slice of the same asset).
expectedBehavior.source: Implied by AssetStatePeriod definition ('a time span when an asset has the same qty/amount/MRR'; one period per state); note: official docs do not state non-overlap explicitly - flagged as documentation gap

scenarioResults.matchSummary: PARTIAL MATCH. The core amendment period-split mechanic IS working correctly on the clean cases (07DSnFYAW and 08MuWnYAK: prior period closed at effective date, new contiguous period with changed qty/mrr) - independently re-queried and confirmed. However observed behavior does NOT fully match expected: (1) 08DFvvYAG's latest period and the asset itself have EndDate/LifecycleEndDate=null on a TERMED (non-evergreen) product - invalid open-ended period; (2) same-day amendments on 08deyfYAA/08deygYAA produce NO split at all (single period with final totals), contradicting 'one period per asset action'; (3) all 26 lifecycle periods have SegmentType=null instead of a populated value. IMPORTANT CORRECTION to the evidence bundle: the claimed 'overlapping periods on 08LXfZYAW' is NOT real - re-querying ordered by StartDate shows the three periods tile contiguously with no overlap; that finding should be retracted (the real 08LXfZYAW defects are mrr=0 on the renewal year and asset Current qty/mrr=0). Sample is thin (only 16 live lifecycle AssetActions in the org; ~430k rows are bulk migration) - conclusions rest on those 16 and should say so.

Per Salesforce docs, null EndDate on the last period is valid ONLY for evergreen subscriptions. Add a validation/backfill to detect null EndDate on non-evergreen assets before license-key processing consumes it.

observedBehavior.whatHappened: KEY NUANCE not spelled out in the bundle: the native uplift mechanism is entirely UNUSED. The renewal MRR uplift seen on 06t/08ARwnYAG is therefore NOT produced by native PriceRevisionPolicy/UnitPriceUplift — it is a raw new Mrr value written by Fortra's upstream COLA/renewal pricing (SC-3346/SC-3350 stack). scenarioResults.matchSummary: SC-3506's core claim about native renewal Asset State Period behavior is VALIDATED against live FortraUAT and matches the documented Salesforce model: every renewal (AssetAction Type=Change / CategoryEnum=Renewals) creates a NEW, forward-dated AssetStatePeriod whose StartDate is exactly the day after the prior period's EndDate, preserving the prior period and carrying the renewal quantity — confirmed on all 4 renewal assets by independent re-query, plus the documented 'cancellation creates no new period' confirmed on the renew-then-cancel asset. I independently reproduced every population count in the bundle to the record (ASP 430642, AA 430646, Change/Renewals=5). The renewal ASP-GENERATION mechanism is behaving correctly. The three flagged anomalies are real and confirmed but are UPSTREAM of ASP generation, not ASP-engine defects: (a) the 2039 12-year EndDate on 06tCOTYA2 is a term/date-derivation defect that the ASP faithfully persisted and then propagated to Asset.LifecycleEndDate; (b) the mrr=0 renewal periods on 08FcLaYAK/08LXfZYAW are the known COLA renewal zero-price defects (SC-3350/SC-3346) — the ASP row is structurally correct (right dates/qty), only the upstream-supplied price is $0. Two important nuances the bundle understates: (1) the native PriceRevisionPolicy/UnitPriceUplift uplift mechanism is entirely UNUSED org-wide (0 PriceRevisionPolicy records; 0 ASPs with UnitPriceUplift or PriceRevisionPolicyId), so all renewal uplifts are upstream-computed raw Mrr, not native uplift — the ASP layer cannot be the uplift owner; (2) a new finding: 08LXfZYAW's Asset current-state pointer (CurrentQuantity/CurrentMrr=0) is desynced from its own live non-zero period, which directly threatens the ticket's license-key-reads-latest-state-period dependency. Caveat: the empirical base is only 5 renewals (all others are migration), so conclusions on renewal behavior are structurally sound but statistically thin.

scenarioResults.scenario: Peer review of SC-3506's claim about CANCELLATION Asset State Period behavior in native RLM / Revenue Cloud Advanced (RCA), validated against the org's only live cancellation in FortraUAT — asset beSECURE 02iWC000008ARwoYAG (short segment 08ARwoYAG), which ran the Generate -> Renewal -> Cancel sequence. Scope: (1) establish documented expected cancellation behavior with official Salesforce citations; (2) independently re-query the live asset's AssetStatePeriod, AssetAction, and Asset lifecycle fields to verify observed behavior; (3) assess the edge case where the immediately-preceding Renewal (AA-000543545) left no renewal state period and whether the cancel rolled it back. Sample size n=1 (the only Cancel/Cancellations AssetAction in the org).

expectedBehavior.rule: A cancellation produces an AssetAction with Type=Cancel and CategoryEnum=Cancellations carrying a negative quantity delta (QuantityChange = -1 for a single-unit asset), reversing the asset's active quantity.
expectedBehavior.source: Salesforce Trailhead — Asset Lifecycle Management with Revenue Cloud, 'Manage Customer Asset Renewals and Cancellations' (cancellation = negative quantity, e.g. -1): https://trailhead.salesforce.com/content/learn/modules/asset-lifecycle-management-with-revenue-cloud/manage-customer-asset-renewals-and-cancellations . Live picklist from sf sobject describe AssetAction confirms Type includes Cancel and CategoryEnum includes Cancellations (SC-3506 bundle section 1).

expectedBehavior.rule: A renewal ADDS a new forward-dated AssetStatePeriod, but a cancellation does NOT create a new AssetStatePeriod; the existing period is closed/end-dated and the asset's current quantity/MRR are driven to zero. Time-slicing model: OrderItem -> AssetActionSource -> AssetAction -> Asset, sliced by AssetStatePeriod.
expectedBehavior.source: Repo synthesis of official docs — OFFICIAL_RCA_REFERENCES.md line 17: 'renewal adds a new state period; cancellation does not.' Anchored to Salesforce RLM Developer Guide (https://resources.docs.salesforce.com/latest/latest/en-us/sfdc/pdf/revenue_lifecycle_management_dev_guide.pdf) and the Trailhead asset-lifecycle module.

expectedBehavior.rule: After cancellation the Asset is left at CurrentQuantity=0 and CurrentMrr=0 (economically zeroed) and lifecycle end reflects closure of the last active period. Asset amend/renew/cancel actions work only for assets created through the standard order-activation lifecycle.
expectedBehavior.source: help.salesforce.com — 'Manage Assets in Revenue Lifecycle Management': https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ind.qocal_manage_assets_in_revenue_lifecycle_management.htm ; 'Amend and Renew Assets with Contract Pricing' (LastTransaction scope = amend/renew): https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ind.qocal_amend_and_renew_assets_with_contract_pricing.htm

expectedBehavior.source: Salesforce RLM Developer Guide AssetAction/AssetActionSource object references: https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.revenue_lifecycle_management_dev_guide.meta/revenue_lifecycle_management_dev_guide/sforce_api_objects_assetactionsource.htm (corroborated by SC-3506 bundle section 1 'fields not editable').

scenarioResults.matchSummary: SC-3506's core cancellation claim is CONFIRMED by independent re-query of the org's only live cancellation. Asset 02iWC000008ARwoYAG has exactly one Cancel/Cancellations AssetAction (AA-000543546, QuantityChange=-1) and NO new AssetStatePeriod was created (COUNT=1, ASP-000543404 only; --all-rows recycle-bin-inclusive also returns 1); the asset is driven to CurrentQuantity=0 / CurrentMrr=0 / CurrentAmount=0. This matches the documented model (renewal adds a state period; cancellation does not) per the RLM Developer Guide and Trailhead asset-lifecycle module. The bundle's numbers are accurate (labeling nuance only: it abbreviates the asset Id to 08ARwoYAG and the period to ASP-404; the real values are 02iWC000008ARwoYAG and ASP-000543404). The one place the bundle overstates certainty is the edge-case 'the cancel rolled back the renewal period': the preceding Renewal AA-000543545 was itself a $0 / qty-unchanged renewal, and no soft-deleted renewal period exists in the recycle bin (--all-rows), so 'rollback removed the renewal period' is plausible but NOT provable from data; 'a $0 renewal never materialized a distinct period' is an equally consistent explanation. Sample is n=1, so no cancellation conclusion should be treated as statistically robust.

gaps.description: The bundle (section 4) asserts the immediately-preceding Renewal AA-000543545 'left no renewal state period... the cancel appears to have removed/rolled back the just-created future renewal period.' Independent verification cannot confirm the rollback mechanism. The renewal AA-000543545 was a ZERO-value renewal (MrrChange=0, QuantityChange=0, TotalMrr=0) — unlike the two control renewals (Abstract +0.30 MRR, and 08FcLaYAK) which each DID create a second period. Crucially, --all-rows (recycle-bin inclusive) returns only 1 AssetStatePeriod for the cancel asset (IsDeleted=false), and the control renewal assets show no soft-deleted period rows either. So either (a) the cancel hard-deleted the renewal's period bypassing the recycle bin, or (b) the $0/qty-unchanged renewal never materialized a distinct forward-dated period at all. The data cannot distinguish these.
gaps.evidence: AA-000543545: Type=Change, CategoryEnum=Renewals, QuantityChange=0, MrrChange=0, TotalMrr=0, IsDeleted=false (still present). Cancel asset AssetStatePeriod --all-rows COUNT=1 (ASP-000543404 only, IsDeleted=false). Contrast: Abstract renewal AA-000543544 MrrChange=+0.30 produced ASP-000543544; 08FcLaYAK renewal produced ASP-000543548.
gaps.recommendation: Reframe from 'cancel rolled back the renewal period' to 'the renew-then-cancel sequence left only the original (now-closed) period; the mechanism (hard-delete vs. no-period-ever-created for a $0 renewal) is undetermined from data.' To resolve, run a NEW controlled test: renew an asset with a non-zero uplift (so the renewal provably creates a period), confirm the period exists, THEN cancel and re-query with --all-rows to isolate whether cancel deletes an existing renewal period.

gaps.description: The entire cancellation conclusion rests on n=1 (the single Cancel/Cancellations AssetAction in the org; bundle section 2 GROUP BY shows Cancel=1). One data point cannot demonstrate behavior across cancellation variants (partial/quantity-decrement vs full, mid-term vs end-of-term, cancel of an amended/upsold asset, cancel WITHOUT a preceding renewal, multi-line/bundle cancel). SC-3506 acceptance criterion #2 ('verify current implementation matches expected RCA behavior') is only weakly satisfiable at n=1, and the one sample is atypical (preceded by a $0 renewal).
gaps.evidence: AssetAction GROUP BY Type/CategoryEnum: only 1 Cancel row org-wide. That cancel is preceded by a $0 renewal, making it an edge scenario rather than a clean baseline cancel.
gaps.recommendation: Explicitly state the n=1 limitation in the SC-3506 deliverable. Generate additional cancellation test cases (minimum: a clean full cancel of a never-renewed asset, and a partial quantity cancel) before declaring the cancellation path validated. A clean full-cancel gives the true baseline the current edge-case sample lacks.

gaps.description: The one observed cancel has MrrChange=0 and TotalCancellationsAmount=0, so it does NOT exercise the negative/credit economics of cancellation (documented negative Net Total credit shape; and the SC-3441 defect where cancel lines show USD 0.00 instead of a negative amount). This record validates the STRUCTURAL state-period rule but says nothing about cancellation PRICING correctness.
gaps.evidence: AA-000543546 MrrChange=0, TotalCancellationsAmount=0; asset was already Mrr=0 pre-cancel (ASP-000543404 Mrr=0). Related known issue tracked in Jira/Task/sc3441 (07_DEEP_RESEARCH_NATIVE_CANCELLATION.md).
gaps.recommendation: Scope SC-3506's cancellation validation to state-period/lifecycle STRUCTURE only, and cross-reference SC-3441 for cancellation credit pricing rather than implying this single record validates cancellation economics. Include a non-zero-priced cancel in the additional test cases (G2) to observe TotalCancellationsAmount and MrrChange<0.

gaps.description: After cancellation the Asset.Status remained 'Installed' rather than transitioning to a distinct cancelled/terminated status, even though CurrentQuantity=0 and CurrentMrr=0. Downstream consumers — notably the LKG license-key framework, which per bundle section 5 keys off the latest state period's expiration/entitlement — that filter or gate on Asset.Status='Installed' could mistake a fully-cancelled asset for an active one; they must rely on CurrentQuantity=0 or an elapsed LifecycleEndDate instead.
gaps.evidence: Asset 02iWC000008ARwoYAG: Status=Installed, CurrentQuantity=0, CurrentMrr=0, LifecycleEndDate=2026-06-10T23:59:59Z (in the past).
gaps.recommendation: Confirm whether 'Installed with qty 0' is the intended RCA terminal state for a cancelled asset (appears to be native behavior, not a defect) and ensure license-key/entitlement logic treats CurrentQuantity=0 (or elapsed LifecycleEndDate) — not Status — as the cancellation signal. Document this explicitly for the license-key dependency in SC-3506's motivation.

claims.claim: An AssetStatePeriod represents a time span during which an asset holds the SAME quantity, amount, and monthly recurring revenue (MRR). Verbatim from the RLM Developer Guide object reference: 'Represents a time span when an asset has the same quantity, amount, and monthly recurring revenue (MRR). An asset has as many asset state periods as there are changes to it (asset actions) during its lifecycle.' Thus the count of state periods on an asset equals the number of state-changing asset actions over its lifecycle.
claims.source: Salesforce RLM Developer Guide — AssetStatePeriod object reference (developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.revenue_lifecycle_management_dev_guide.meta/.../sforce_api_objects_assetstateperiod.htm), fetched verbatim; corroborated by object_reference variant and WebSearch abstracts

claims.claim: Key AssetStatePeriod fields and their documented meaning: StartDate/EndDate (datetime bounds of the period; EndDate is null for an evergreen subscription's final/open-ended period), Quantity (total qty during the period), Mrr (MRR during the period), Amount (asset total amount during the period — noted as 'currently unused by Revenue Cloud'), UnitPrice (per-unit price; NOT populated in API v66.0+), UnitPriceUplift (percentage increase of the unit price), Discount (0–100 percent), SegmentType (period type: Custom / Free Trial / Yearly), and PriceRevisionPolicy (lookup to the price-uplift policy for the period). Available API v50.0+.
claims.source: Salesforce RLM Developer Guide — AssetStatePeriod object reference, field-by-field extract (fetched)

claims.claim: The documented lifecycle object chain is OrderItem (Order Product) → AssetActionSource → AssetAction → Asset, with the Asset time-sliced by one or more AssetStatePeriod rows. When assets are created or modified from an order, the system generates an AssetStatePeriod ('the state of an asset over a period of time') and an AssetAction ('the change made to an asset'), and each AssetAction records the change in quantity, amount, and MRR.
claims.source: Salesforce Subscription Management Guide — Renew Subscription Example (developer.salesforce.com/docs/revenue/subscription-management/guide/solution-renew.html), fetched; AssetAction/AssetActionSource object references via WebSearch abstracts

claims.claim: AssetAction 'represents a change made to a lifecycle-managed asset' (fields not editable, API v50.0+). AssetActionSource is 'an optional way to record what transactions caused changes to lifecycle-managed assets ... to trace financial and other information about asset actions,' supporting Salesforce order products, work order line items, and external-system transaction IDs. AssetActionSource is the provenance link from the driving OrderItem/transaction to the AssetAction; it is optional but is what populates when order-to-asset runs from an Order.
claims.source: Salesforce Object Reference / RLM Developer Guide — AssetAction and AssetActionSource (WebSearch verbatim abstracts of developer.salesforce.com object reference pages)

claims.claim: INITIAL SALE: the first assetization of a given (Account, Product) generates one AssetAction (Type=Generate, business category Initial Sale) and one initial AssetStatePeriod carrying the sold quantity, MRR, and start/end dates. The standard action createOrUpdateAssetFromOrder creates new assets for a new order and updates existing assets for change orders (renewal/cancellation), matching one Asset per (Account, Product).
claims.source: Subscription Management Renew Example (fetched) + createOrUpdateAssetFromOrder action reference (abstract); live-org describe in internal evidence bundle confirms AssetAction.Type={Generate,Change,Cancel,Convert} and CategoryEnum includes 'Initial Sale'

claims.claim: AMENDMENT (upsell/downsell/quantity change): a NEW AssetStatePeriod is created that reflects the updated quantity/amount/MRR, effective on the amendment's take-effect date; the prior period is bounded (end-dated) at that effective date so the timeline is contiguous (an effective-date split). Trailhead verbatim: 'You also see a new asset state period (2) that reflects the updated quantity for the current period.' The change is recorded as an AssetAction with a business category such as Upsells/Downsells (verbatim: 'a new asset action appears with the business category set to Upsells'). Quantity is entered as a delta (e.g. +8, or -3 for a removal).
claims.source: Trailhead — Managing Customer Asset Amendments in Revenue Cloud (fetched verbatim); live-org observations in internal evidence bundle (SC-3506/3522) show prior period EndDate truncated to amendment date + new next-day period with new qty

claims.claim: RENEWAL: a NEW forward-dated AssetStatePeriod is created reflecting the updated renewal dates, quantity, and MRR, and a NEW AssetAction (business category Renewals) is created to record the change; the original/prior period is left unchanged. Subscription Management example verbatim: 'The original asset state period is unchanged.' / 'A new asset state period is created. It's start date is Jan 1, 2023.' / 'A new asset action is created to record the change in quantity, amount, and MRR due to the renewal.' Trailhead verbatim: 'a new Asset Start[e] Period is generated to reflect the updated renewal dates.'
claims.source: Subscription Management Renew Example (fetched verbatim) + Trailhead Manage Customer Asset Renewals and Cancellations (fetched verbatim)

claims.claim: RENEWAL OPTIONS: two documented renewal modes — (1) Automatic Renewal, which extends the subscription automatically at the end of the current term based on the asset's predefined renewal term; and (2) Override Renewal Term, which configures a custom renewal period by setting specific start and end dates (and can generate a quote/order to refund an unused portion).
claims.source: Trailhead — Manage Customer Asset Renewals and Cancellations (fetched verbatim)

claims.claim: CANCELLATION: unlike amendments and renewals, NO new AssetStatePeriod is created for a cancellation. Trailhead verbatim: 'However, unlike amendments and renewals, a new Asset State Period isn't created for cancellations.' A cancellation is recorded as an AssetAction (business category Cancellations); the cancel quote uses a negative quantity delta (e.g. -1) to drive End Quantity to 0. The prior period simply remains/closes; the asset's current quantity and MRR go to 0.
claims.source: Trailhead — Manage Customer Asset Renewals and Cancellations (fetched verbatim); live-org evidence bundle confirms Cancel action created zero new AssetStatePeriod

claims.claim: RENEWAL PRICE UPLIFT — FIXED: UnitPriceUplift is a flat percentage increase to the unit price for a subscription. A sales rep can specify the uplift percentage on the quote line item; it carries through OrderItem to the AssetStatePeriod when the order is activated, so the renewal period's price reflects the uplift (AssetStatePeriod.UnitPriceUplift = 'Percentage increase of a line item's unit price').
claims.source: AssetStatePeriod object reference (fetched, UnitPriceUplift field) + The Cloud Update 'Fixed vs CPI-Based Uplift' + WebSearch abstracts

claims.claim: RENEWAL PRICE UPLIFT — CPI / POLICY-DRIVEN: PriceRevisionPolicy is a lookup (present on QLI, Order Product, and AssetStatePeriod) that defines a CPI/index-based renewal uplift. The renewal net unit price is computed as Last Transaction Price × (1 + CPI rate + defined renewal uplift %). Example: $150 × (1 + 0.045 + 0.03) = $161.25; a July-2025 renewal at 2.7% CPI + 5% spread = 7.7%. Requires Last Transaction Pricing on the asset and term-based subscriptions; if asset pricing source is List Price the uplift is ignored.
claims.source: WebSearch verbatim abstracts of Salesforce Help 'Use Consumer Price Index for Automated Renewal Price Uplifts' + The Cloud Update renewal-uplift article; corroborated by AssetStatePeriod.PriceRevisionPolicy field in dev guide

claims.claim: AssetAction picklists (live-org describe, FortraUAT): Type = {Generate, Change, Cancel, Convert}; CategoryEnum = {Initial Sale, Upsells, Downsells, Cross-Sells, Cancellations, Transfers, Terms And Conditions Changes, Renewals, Upgrades, Downgrades, Swaps, Other}; Subtype includes FieldAmendment, plus delta fields QuantityChange, MrrChange, Amount, SubtotalChange and running totals (TotalQuantity, TotalMrr, TotalRenewalsAmount, etc.). This resolves the SC-3419 'UNCONFIRMED picklist literals': official docs collapse amendments into a single 'Amendments' concept, but the platform splits them into Upsells/Downsells/Cross-Sells/Upgrades/Downgrades/Swaps/Terms And Conditions Changes; Type adds Convert and Cancel beyond Generate/Change.
claims.source: Internal evidence bundle (SC-3506/SC-3522) captured live via sf sobject describe on FortraUAT 2026-07-01

claims.claim: Practical significance for license-key processing (the SC-3506 motivation): because renewals and amendments each create a NEW AssetStatePeriod carrying the current/latest quantity and dates while cancellations create none, downstream consumers that key off the 'latest state period' must read the most-recent-effective AssetStatePeriod for correct expiration date and entitlement quantity. Observed live-org anomalies (renewal EndDate landing in 2039, mrr=0 renewals, and a renew-then-cancel that left no renewal period) are deviations from this expected model, not the model itself.

verdicts.correction:

1) BoKS-NewMaintenance is NOT a termed product. Its only ProductSellingModelOption is "One Time" (SellingModelType=OneTime, null PricingTerm), and all 40 OrderItems for it are OneTime. For a OneTime line, RCA does not stamp a term EndDate on the state period, so ASP EndDate=null is the correct, expected native behavior - not a bug in the FieldAmendment/upsell path.

2) The premise "null EndDate is valid ONLY for evergreen" is unsupported by any cited Salesforce doc and is contradicted by the org: ~42% of all ASP rows (181,955) have null EndDate, including on OneTime AND TermDefined-capable products. So null EndDate does not, by itself, indicate a defect.

Recommendation to force a bounded ASP EndDate on this asset (and validate/backfill non-evergreen assets) is misdirected as written - it would fight correct native OneTime behavior. Reframe the finding as a business/design question: license-key expiration for OneTime maintenance lines cannot be derived from the ASP EndDate (correctly null); if an expiration date is required, source it from the parent Contract end (Contract 800WC00000S3fOLYAZ EndDate = 2027-06-04, ContractTerm=12) or from a dedicated term field, and confirm with the LKG framework owners whether OneTime maintenance keys even need an expiration. The specific date 2027-06-04 in the recommendation is coincidentally the real Contract end, which supports pursuing the Contract-sourced approach rather than mutating the ASP.

This proves the split discriminator is NOT transaction/calendar day (08MuWnYAK's two actions were BOTH created on the same calendar day yet it split); it is whether the amendment's EFFECTIVE date equals the asset's start/born date. When amendment effective date == asset start date, there is no non-degenerate prior time-slice to preserve, so native RLM correctly keeps one period. Repo official reference (Jira/Task/sc3419/evidence/W1_rlm_asset_lifecycle.md) describes AssetStatePeriod as date-driven time-slices where new periods reflect updated dates - consistent with a date-driven, not action-count-driven, split model.
verdicts.correction: The underlying data (one period, final q3, born-day CreatedDate, in-place LastModified) is exactly as stated and CONFIRMED. But the claim's diagnosis is overstated/mislabeled on two points: (1) The trigger is NOT 'same-day' transaction timing. The comparison asset 08MuWnYAK had BOTH its Generate and Upsell AssetActions created on the same calendar day (2026-06-16, ~1h apart) and it DID split. So the real discriminator is amendment EFFECTIVE date vs. asset START date: 08MuWnYAK's install was backdated to 04-01 while its amendment took effect 06-16 (distinct -> split), whereas 08deyf/08deyg were born and amended both effective 06-29 (identical -> no split). (2) It does NOT 'contradict the documented model' nor is it 'inconsistent with the correct split.' It is the SAME date-driven time-slicing rule: an amendment whose effective date equals the asset's start date produces a zero-length prior slice, which RLM legitimately folds into a single period. This is intentional/expected native RLM behavior, matching the very hypothesis in the claim's own RECOMMENDATION ('amendment effective date == asset start date means no distinct prior slice'). Recommended reclassification: NOT a high-severity gap/contradiction; document it as an EXPECTED native exception (no split when amendment effective date == asset born date) and, as the claim rightly notes, ensure license-key logic reads the latest state period's attributes and handles the single-period case. Minor: sample is only 2 same-effective-date events (both Cobalt Strike + beSECURE from one 6/29 order), so the rule is empirically supported but thin.

verdicts.evidence:
All numeric/data facts independently re-queried on FortraUAT (00DWC000006eUFF2A2) and CONFIRMED exactly.

(1) Org-wide SegmentType distribution — `SELECT SegmentType, COUNT(Id) FROM AssetStatePeriod GROUP BY SegmentType` -> null=921, Yearly=429721. Exact match.

(2) The 14 lifecycle assets were derived from `SELECT AssetId,Type,CategoryEnum,Subtype FROM AssetAction WHERE Type!='Generate'` (16 rows across 14 distinct assets; 08ARwoYAG and 08LXfZYAW appear twice). `SELECT SegmentType,COUNT(Id) FROM AssetStatePeriod WHERE AssetId IN (<14 ids>) GROUP BY SegmentType` -> null=26, and no non-null bucket. So 26 null / 0 non-null, exact match. Row-level dump of all 26 confirms every SegmentType=null.

(3) Independent single-asset re-queries (task requirement): 08MuWnYAK -> ASP-000543598 & ASP-000543602 both SegmentType=null; 08deyfYAA -> ASP-000543851 null; 08deygYAA -> ASP-000543852 null; also 07DSnFYAW, 08DFvvYAG, 08LXfZYAW all null in the bulk dump.

(4) Provenance: `SELECT CreatedBy.Name,COUNT(Id) ... WHERE SegmentType='Yearly' GROUP BY CreatedBy.Name` -> Marc DeBrey created 429,611 of the 429,721 Yearly rows, consistent with a bulk install-base migration load. Native lifecycle periods (created by German Wren, Sachin Gupta, Nir Kailash, Aaron Broom, Liam Jeong, Marc DeBrey, etc.) are null.

CONFIRMED: the empirical core (26 null lifecycle periods, 921 vs 429,721 org-wide, migrated=Yearly) is exactly right.

REFUTING/QUALIFYING evidence against the claim's FRAMING:
(A) Null SegmentType is NOT specific to amend/renew/cancel lifecycle periods. `SELECT COUNT(Id) FROM AssetStatePeriod WHERE SegmentType=null AND AssetId NOT IN (<14 ids>)` -> 895 additional null periods, CreatedDate 2026-01-28..2026-07-01. `SELECT COUNT_DISTINCT(AssetId) WHERE SegmentType=null` -> 909 distinct assets carry null periods, not 14. Sampling 5 of those other null assets, `SELECT AssetId,Type,CategoryEnum FROM AssetAction` shows all are Type=Generate/CategoryEnum='Initial Sale' — i.e. plain new-business assets with NO amendment, yet still null. So native RLM leaves SegmentType null on ALL runtime-generated periods (Initial Sale generation included), and the 26 are just the amend/renew subset.
(B) The 'Yearly = picklist default' characterization is unsupported and arguably contradicted: if Yearly were an auto-applied field default, native period creation would yield Yearly, but every natively-created period (Initial Sale, upsell, renewal) is null. The Yearly values are explicit migration-load values. The actual picklist default value could not be verified via read-only data query (sobject describe was disallowed).
verdicts.correction: The data is exactly correct; the interpretation is slightly overstated/mis-scoped in two ways. First, null SegmentType is not a property of amendment/renewal/cancellation generation specifically — it is a property of ALL native RLM-generated AssetStatePeriods, including Generate/Initial-Sale new-business periods. There are 921 null periods across 909 distinct assets; the 26 on the 14 amend/renew/cancel assets are just the subset the review sampled. The real dividing line is bulk data-migration load (SegmentType='Yearly', ~429,721, loaded under Marc DeBrey's user) vs. any native runtime creation (SegmentType=null). This actually STRENGTHENS the gap (broader footprint) but the recommendation should target the native generation path generally (and/or a global backfill of the 921 rows), not just the amend/renew path. Second, calling 'Yearly' "the picklist default" is not supported by the data and is likely inaccurate: native creation would produce the default if one applied, yet it produces null; 'Yearly' is best described as the migration-load value, not an auto-default. The gap itself (native periods carry null SegmentType, inconsistent with the migrated Yearly convention; risk if any downstream billing/license-key/reporting logic branches on SegmentType) is valid and the remediation direction (determine expected SegmentType, populate in generation path or backfill, confirm no consumer treats null as significant) is sound. Note also that per the evidence bundle's own LKG analysis, no current consumer was found reading SegmentType, so the medium severity is a forward-looking/consistency risk rather than a confirmed live break.

verdicts.evidence:
Independently re-queried FortraUAT (00DWC000006eUFF2A2 = alias FortraUAT, verified in `sf org list`). All queries read-only.

(1) 08LXfZYAW ASP-566 mrr=0 — CONFIRMED EXACTLY. Query: `SELECT AssetStatePeriodNumber, StartDate, EndDate, Quantity, Mrr FROM AssetStatePeriod WHERE AssetId='02iWC000008LXfZYAW' ORDER BY StartDate ASC` returned:
- ASP-000543561 2026-07-01->2026-07-31 q100 mrr162.5
- ASP-000543568 2026-08-01->2027-06-30 q275 mrr162.5
- ASP-000543566 2027-07-01->2028-06-30 q275 mrr=0
ASP-566 has the LATEST StartDate (2027-07-01) of the three, so the mrr=0 period IS the forward-most/"latest" period — the claim's "latest period" characterization holds.

(2) 08FcLaYAK ASP-548 mrr=0 from 557.94 — CONFIRMED EXACTLY. Query on ASP-000543543/548 returned: ASP-543 2026-06-11->2027-06-10 q1 mrr=557.9416666666667 (source period) -> ASP-548 2027-06-11->2028-06-10 q1 mrr=0 (renewal period). Exactly the 557.94->0 drop stated.

(3) Both zero-MRR periods are genuinely RENEWAL-generated (not migration/upsell). Query: `SELECT AssetActionNumber, Type, CategoryEnum, MrrChange, TotalMrr, CreatedDate FROM AssetAction WHERE CategoryEnum='Renewals' ORDER BY CreatedDate ASC` returned 5 renewals. AA-000543549 (08FcLaYAK, Change/Renewals, MrrChange=-557.94, TotalMrr=0, created 2026-06-11T18:40:36) matches ASP-548's CreatedDate/asset exactly; AA-000543567 (08LXfZYAW, Change/Renewals, MrrChange=-162.5, TotalMrr=0, created 2026-06-15T20:32:21) matches ASP-566's CreatedDate/asset exactly. Both renewals fully reverse the prior MRR to zero (MrrChange = -priorMrr).

(4) Zero-MRR is anomalous, NOT expected renewal behavior. The SAME renewal query shows 2 of 5 renewals renewed CORRECTLY with positive uplifted MRR: AA-000000083 (06tCOTYA2 TotalMrr=32.2875, +1.5375 COLA uplift) and AA-000543544 (08ARwnYAG TotalMrr=4.13425, +0.30 uplift). So a correct renewal produces a positive COLA-uplifted MRR; the two flagged assets do not. This contrast confirms the zero is a defect, not the design.

(5) SC-3350/SC-3346 linkage is well-founded. Auto-memory project_cola_renewal_pricing_review documents SC-3350/3346 as the COLA renewal zero-price defect (renewal quotes commit NetUnitPrice=0/TotalPrice=0; the SC-3350 net-seed fix was deleted by the SC-3346 rework on 06-13/14, reproducing 100% on fresh renewals). The zero-MRR renewal ASPs are the downstream asset-lifecycle manifestation of that same $0-net renewal-pricing family.
verdicts.correction:
The gap is factually correct and well-supported; two minor scoping refinements (do not change the CONFIRMED verdict):

(a) "would feed wrong entitlement/pricing into license processing" is slightly overstated for MRR specifically. The evidence bundle's own Section 5 establishes that Fortra's LKG (license-key) framework does NOT read AssetStatePeriod.Mrr — it consumes expiration/StartDate + quantity (grep shows only StartDate referenced, 3x). So the direct license-key risk is date/quantity-driven, and the MRR=0 is a pricing/entitlement-value corruption whose license-key impact is business-process-level, not a direct field read. The RECOMMENDATION already reframes this correctly as "not an ASP-mechanics bug but a pricing-derivation bug," so the recommendation is sound even though the impact sentence is broader than the evidence strictly supports.

(b) The two assets differ in severity at the Asset roll-up level, worth noting for the writeup: 08LXfZYAW has Asset.CurrentMrr=0 (fully zeroed). 08FcLaYAK still has Asset.CurrentMrr=557.94 (the zero is confined to the future renewal period ASP-548 while the current period ASP-543 retains 557.94). Both have PricingSource=null, which is the same null-PricingSource condition the SC-3350 RCA identified as a root contributor to the waterfall net=0. This reinforces, not weakens, the SC-3350/3346 linkage.

verdicts.correction: The gap is accurate and, if anything, understated on two points — both strengthen it, not weaken it. (A) AA-000543545 is not merely "a zero-value renewal" relative to the two named controls; it is the UNIQUE renewal in the entire org with BOTH QuantityChange=0 AND MrrChange=0. All four other renewals (incl. two beyond the controls the gap cited, AA-000000083 and AA-000543567) had non-zero MRR deltas and each created a forward period. This makes hypothesis (b) — a genuinely no-op renewal produces no new state period — even more plausible as the innocent explanation, so the bundle's "cancel rolled back the period" is the less-supported reading. (B) The gap frames the recycle-bin miss as "either cancel hard-deleted bypassing the bin, or no period was ever created." An additional org-wide fact makes even the "hard-delete" leg unprovable-by-absence: there are ZERO soft-deleted AssetActions and ZERO soft-deleted AssetStatePeriods anywhere in the org, and RLM's cancel emitted no Subtype=Rollback action — i.e., there is no evidence RLM ever routes lifecycle deletes through the recycle bin at all, so the empty recycle bin is not affirmative evidence against a hard-delete and is not affirmative evidence for it. The bundle should therefore drop the causal verb "rolled back" (which implies a rollback mechanism that does not exist in the data) and restate as: "the renew-then-cancel sequence left only the original, now-closed period; whether the $0/qty-unchanged renewal ever materialized a distinct forward period cannot be determined from n=1." The recommended controlled test (renew with a provable non-zero uplift, confirm the forward period exists, THEN cancel and re-query with --all-rows) is the correct and necessary way to resolve it.

RLM expresses cancellation via qty/MRR->0 on the current period and via AssetActions, not via the Status picklist; Status is a legacy general-purpose Asset field outside the lifecycle-management field set. verdicts.correction: The GAP's DOWNSTREAM-IMPACT framing and its recommended remediation are OVERSTATED/INACCURATE about how the actual LKG code behaves. (1) The GAP says the LKG framework 'per bundle section 5 keys off the latest state period's expiration/entitlement.' Production LKG code does NOT reference AssetStatePeriod, CurrentQuantity, or CurrentMrr anywhere (grep of all non-test Lkg*.cls confirms zero hits). (2) The only Status gate in the entire LKG framework is an OPTIONAL, caller-supplied statusFilter in the UI list-picker LkgUiHardwareController.getAssets (line 92: whereClause += ' AND Status = :statusFilter'); the key-generation path (LkgProcessorHardwareKeys) applies NO Status filter. So the 'mistake a cancelled asset for active' risk is real but confined to a UI picker only if a caller passes 'Installed' -- it is NOT a systemic key-gen gating bug. (3) Most important: the GAP recommends consumers 'rely on CurrentQuantity=0' -- but LkgProcessorHardwareKeys.cls line 241 reads Asset.Quantity (which is STILL 1 on this cancelled asset, confirmed by live query), NOT CurrentQuantity (=0). Therefore CurrentQuantity=0 would NOT actually protect the production LKG path as written; the code would first have to be changed to read CurrentQuantity/current-period. The only cancellation signal the production LKG hardware path currently reads that DOES move on cancel is Asset.LifecycleEndDate (line 243), which is elapsed here -- so of the two signals the GAP names, only 'elapsed LifecycleEndDate' is a valid protection for the code as it exists today. Recommend rewording SC-3506's motivation to: (a) state that native RLM has no Status transition on cancel (documented, not a defect); (b) note the base Asset.Quantity field stays at 1 and must not be used as an activity signal; (c) direct LKG/entitlement logic to gate on CurrentQuantity>0 (requiring a code change from the current Asset.Quantity read) and/or LifecycleEndDate in the future, and to remove/avoid any Status='Installed' filter as an active-asset proxy.
